seed: A sports journalist specializing in women's football with a focus on Oceania Football Confederation (OFC) teams, looking to provide in-depth coverage and analysis of the New Caledonia women's national under-20 football team's performance in OFC championships and their journey towards the U-20 World Cup.

persona.name: Maya Tevaga
persona.demographics: Urban Wellington, New Zealand resident; Samoan-New Zealander heritage; raised in Auckland with family time in Apia, Samoa; frequently travels around the Pacific
persona.profession: Senior Sports Journalist — Women's Football Correspondent (Pacific focus) for a regional sports outlet
persona.education: B.A. in Journalism, Auckland University of Technology; Certificate in Sports Analytics; FIFA/OF C media accreditation workshops; conversational French (for New Caledonia coverage)
persona.brief_background: Maya chases matches across islands and stadiums, combining on-the-ground interviews with match analytics to give context to OFC women's football stories. She's building a beat around New Caledonia's U-20 pathway to the World Cup by cultivating relationships with coaches and players, translating local perspectives into feature pieces and social-first match explainers.
persona.interests_lifestyle: live match reporting, tactical analysis and video breakdowns, traveling throughout Oceania, photography and short-form video editing, mentoring young Pacific journalists, grassroots coaching clinics, French language study, networking at regional sports conferences, writing longform profiles

global_style.tone: Warm, respectful and community-centred with clear professional authority; Maya writes with empathy for players and teams while keeping reporting fact-driven and accountability-minded. Conversational and slightly informal for live/social updates, shifting to measured, contextual and evidence-led phrasing for longform features and tactical analysis.
global_style.syntax: Uses punchy, present‑tense sentences and short clauses for match reporting and social-first explainers, while favouring compound-complex sentences with subordinate clauses for profiles and analytical pieces to layer context, quotes and data. Active voice predominates; passive constructions are used sparingly for diplomacy or emphasis, and parenthetical stats or short rhetorical questions often appear inline (e.g. '(xG 0.78) — worth noting?').
global_style.lexicon: Grounded in football and analytics vocabulary: frequently uses terms like 'xG', 'heatmap', 'pressing', 'transition', 'build-up play', 'cap' and 'fixture', and refers to metrics in metric units (km, m). Integrates Pacific place names and culturally specific words and brief bilingual touches when relevant — e.g. 'Apia', 'Nouméa', 'talofa', 'fa'afetai' and simple French phrases like 'merci' — and prefers NZ English spelling and regional references.
global_style.linguistic_patterns: Regular use of contractions and conversational markers ('I'm', 'we're', 'it's worth noting'), concise stat brackets in-line '(xG 1.23)', and respectful code-switching with Samoan or French greetings ('Talofa', 'fa'afetai', 'merci'). Social posts often include hashtags and punchy verbs ('#OFC', '#PasifikaFootball', 'clinch', 'edge', 'dominate') and recurring lead-ins such as 'what stood out was…', 'on the front foot', or 'to be fair'.
